{"type":"text","timestamp":1794722609091,"sessionID":"ses_e223cb74affe5rWPCjKE5Tc6LZ","part":{"id":"prt_1ddcdb7ab001rKQ0riB9s3z4to","messageID":"msg_1ddcda775001NjLXnDubfXoJwN","sessionID":"ses_e223cb74affe5rWPCjKE5Tc6LZ","type":"text","text":"The lid now opens the full 0–110° with at least 0.35 mm clearance at every step from 10°, and the final test_fit passed every gate and score check. The original jammed at 37°.\n\n**Cause:** the bottom corner of each lid rib swept into the hinge-side edge of the enclosure rear wall as the lid opened. This happened at the three lid knuckle positions, starting around 38–50°.\n\n**Fix:** I cut a small 45° chamfer into the top edge of the rear wall, on the hinge-facing side, at each of the three lid knuckles. Each cut is about 7.6 mm long (along the hinge axis) and removes about 7.6 mm³ from the enclosure. Only the enclosure was edited, and nothing was added. The lid, ribs, seal band, brackets and pin bores are untouched.\n\n**Test_fit results:**\n- **S3 minimal change:** passed. The total change is 22.7 mm³ removed, about 0.04 % of the two parts. How that compares with the best known fix is graded separately and isn't shown.\n- **S2 printability:** both wall-thickness and overhang checks passed.\n- **G5 seal:** passed with the narrowest contact at 1.665 mm against the 1.5 mm limit, so the margin is only 0.165 mm. The cut stays outside the 1.5 mm inner seal band.\n\nI used one test_fit call, so no cost was charged, and the result has been submitted.","time":{"start":1794722609067,"end":1794722609087}}}
